trials.final_answer:
The two pivotal randomized controlled trials that established the benefit of imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy in adults with anterior-circulation acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion who were last known well 6–24 hours earlier are the **DAWN trial** and the **DEFUSE 3 trial**. Both were published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in early 2018 and led to the expansion of the thrombectomy window from 6 to 24 hours for carefully selected patients.

---

## 1. DAWN Trial (NCT02142283)

**Reference:** Nogueira RG, et al. *Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378:11-21.

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Time window:** 6–24 hours last known well.

**Imaging selection:** Clinical-core mismatch based on age-stratified criteria (not perfusion imaging):
- **Age <80 years:** Core volume ≤50 mL with NIHSS ≥10
- **Age ≥80 years:** Core volume ≤70 mL with NIHSS ≥10

**Population:** 206 patients with occlusion of the intracranial internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery.

**Primary endpoints (coprimary):**
1. Mean score on the utility-weighted modified Rankin scale (mRS) at 90 days (range 0 [death] to 10 [no symptoms])
2. Rate of functional independence (mRS 0–2) at 90 days

**Key findings:**
- **Utility-weighted mRS at 90 days:** Mean score 5.5 in the thrombectomy group vs. 3.4 in the control group (adjusted difference 2.0 points; 95% credible interval 1.1–3.0; posterior probability of superiority >0.999).
- **Functional independence (mRS 0–2):** 49% in the thrombectomy group vs. 13% in the control group (adjusted difference 33 percentage points; 95% credible interval 24–44; posterior probability of superiority >0.999).
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 6% vs. 3% (P=0.50) — no significant difference.
- **90-day mortality:** 19% vs. 18% (P=1.00) — no significant difference.

The trial was stopped early for efficacy after 206 patients were enrolled.

---

## 2. DEFUSE 3 Trial (NCT02586415)

**Reference:** Albers GW, et al. *Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378:699-708.

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Time window:** 6–16 hours last known well.

**Imaging selection:** CT or MR perfusion imaging demonstrating salvageable tissue:
- Initial infarct core <70 mL
- Penumbra-to-core ratio ≥1.8

**Population:** 182 patients with proximal middle-cerebral-artery or internal-carotid-artery occlusion.

**Primary endpoint:** Ordinal score on the modified Rankin scale at 90 days.

**Key findings:**
- **Favorable shift in mRS distribution:** Odds ratio 2.77 (P<0.001) favoring thrombectomy.
- **Functional independence (mRS 0–2):** 45% in the endovascular-therapy group vs. 17% in the medical-therapy group (P<0.001).
- **90-day mortality:** 14% in the endovascular-therapy group vs. 26% in the medical-therapy group (P=0.05).
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 7% vs. 4% (P=0.75) — no significant difference.
- **Serious adverse events:** 43% vs. 53% (P=0.18) — no significant difference.

The trial was also terminated early for efficacy after 182 patients were randomized.

---

## Summary Comparison

| Feature | DAWN | DEFUSE 3 |
|---|---|---|
| **Time window** | 6–24 hours | 6–16 hours |
| **Imaging selection** | Clinical-core mismatch (age-based) | Perfusion imaging (penumbra-to-core ratio ≥1.8, core <70 mL) |
| **N randomized** | 206 | 182 |
| **Functional independence (mRS 0–2)** | 49% vs. 13% | 45% vs. 17% |
| **mRS shift (OR)** | Not reported as OR | 2.77 (P<0.001) |
| **Symptomatic ICH** | 6% vs. 3% (NS) | 7% vs. 4% (NS) |
| **90-day mortality** | 19% vs. 18% (NS) | 14% vs. 26% (P=0.05) |

Both trials demonstrated that imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy significantly improves 90-day functional outcomes compared with medical therapy alone in this late-window population, with no significant increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. These findings established the standard of care for selected patients presenting 6–24 hours after last known well with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion.

Based on the retrieved evidence, the two pivotal randomized controlled trials that established the benefit of imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy in adults with anterior-circulation acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion who were last known well 6–24 hours earlier are the **DAWN trial** and the **DEFUSE 3 trial**. Both were published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in 2018.

### 1. DAWN Trial (Nogueira et al., 2018)
**Full citation:** Nogueira RG, Jadhav AP, Haussen DC, et al. *Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378(1):11-21. (PubMed ID: 29129157)

*   **Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.
*   **Time Window:** 6 to 24 hours from last known well.
*   **Imaging Selection Criteria:** Patients had to have an occlusion of the intracranial internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery (M1 segment). Crucially, they required a **clinical–imaging mismatch** defined by age-stratified criteria comparing the severity of the clinical deficit (NIHSS score) to the volume of the early infarct on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) or CT perfusion (CTP):
    *   Age <80 years: NIHSS ≥10 and infarct volume ≤31 mL; OR NIHSS ≥10 and infarct volume ≤51 mL with at least 10 mL of salvageable tissue.
    *   Age ≥80 years: NIHSS ≥20 and infarct volume ≤51 mL; OR NIHSS ≥10 and infarct volume ≤51 mL with at least 10 mL of salvageable tissue.
*   **Sample Size:** 206 patients randomized (107 to thrombectomy + standard care; 99 to standard care alone).
*   **Primary Endpoints:** Mean score on the utility-weighted modified Rankin Scale (mRS; range 0–10, where 0 = no symptoms and 10 = death) and the rate of functional independence (mRS 0–2) at 90 days.
*   **Results:**
    *   The trial was stopped early for efficacy after a prespecified interim analysis.
    *   **Functional Independence:** 49% of the thrombectomy group achieved an mRS of 0–2 at 90 days, compared with 13% in the control group (adjusted difference, 33 percentage points; posterior probability of superiority >0.999).
    *   **Disability Score:** The mean utility-weighted mRS score was significantly better in the thrombectomy group (5.5) compared with the control group (3.4; adjusted difference, 2.0 points; 95% credible interval, 1.1 to 3.0).
    *   **Safety:** Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly (6% vs. 3%; P=0.50), nor did 90-day mortality (19% vs. 18%; P=1.00).

### 2. DEFUSE 3 Trial (Albers et al., 2018)
**Full citation:** Albers GW, Marks MP, Kemp S, et al. *Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378(7):629-638. (PubMed ID: 29364767)

*   **Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.
*   **Time Window:** 6 to 16 hours from last known well.
*   **Imaging Selection Criteria:** Patients had to have an occlusion of the proximal middle cerebral artery (M1) or internal carotid artery. They required a **perfusion–imaging mismatch** defined by CT perfusion or MRI diffusion/perfusion using automated software (RAPID):
    *   Initial infarct volume <70 mL.
    *   Mismatch ratio (ischemic penumbra volume / infarct core volume) ≥1.8.
    *   Mismatch volume ≥15 mL.
*   **Sample Size:** 182 patients randomized (92 to endovascular therapy + standard medical therapy; 90 to standard medical therapy alone). The trial was terminated early for efficacy.
*   **Primary Endpoint:** Ordinal score on the modified Rankin Scale (mRS; range 0–6) at 90 days.
*   **Results:**
    *   **Functional Independence:** 45% of the endovascular-therapy group achieved an mRS of 0–2 at 90 days, compared with 17% in the medical-therapy group (risk ratio, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.60 to 4.48; P<0.001).
    *   **Disability Score:** Endovascular therapy was associated with a favorable shift in the distribution of mRS scores (unadjusted common odds ratio, 2.77; 95% CI, 1.63 to 4.70; P<0.001; adjusted OR, 3.36; 95% CI, 1.96 to 5.77; P<0.001).
    *   **Safety:** 90-day mortality was lower in the endovascular group (14% vs. 26%; P=0.05). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly (7% vs. 4%; P=0.75).

### Summary of Findings
Both trials demonstrated that **imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy significantly improves 90-day functional outcomes** compared with medical therapy alone in patients with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion presenting 6–24 hours after last known well. The key distinction lies in the selection criteria:
*   **DAWN** used a **clinical–imaging mismatch** (severity of deficit vs. infarct size), allowing for patients with larger infarct cores if their clinical deficit was disproportionately severe.
*   **DEFUSE 3** used a **perfusion–imaging mismatch** (penumbra vs. core volume), requiring a specific ratio and volume of salvageable tissue regardless of clinical severity (provided the core was <70 mL).

These trials established the "tissue window" concept, shifting the paradigm from strict time-based eligibility to imaging-based selection for late-window thrombectomy.

---

## Pivotal Trials Establishing Late-Window Thrombectomy Benefit

Two landmark randomized controlled trials established that **imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy improves 90-day functional outcomes compared with best medical therapy alone** in adults with anterior-circulation acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion presenting 6–24 hours after last known well:

---

### 1. **DAWN Trial** (Nogueira et al., *NEJM* 2018)

**Full title:** *Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct*

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Population:** 206 patients with occlusion of the intracranial internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery, last known well 6–24 hours earlier, with a **clinical–imaging mismatch** (severity of clinical deficit disproportionately large relative to infarct volume). Mismatch criteria were age-stratified:
- **Age <80 years:** infarct volume ≤70 mL with NIHSS ≥10, or infarct volume 70–30 mL with NIHSS ≥20
- **Age ≥80 years:** infarct volume ≤30 mL with NIHSS ≥10

**Intervention:** Thrombectomy plus standard care vs. standard care alone.

**Primary endpoints:**
- Mean score on the **utility-weighted modified Rankin Scale** (0 = death, 10 = no symptoms) at 90 days
- Rate of **functional independence** (mRS 0–2) at 90 days

**Key findings:**
- **Functional independence at 90 days:** **49%** in the thrombectomy group vs. **13%** in the control group (adjusted difference 33 percentage points; posterior probability of superiority >0.999)
- **Mean utility-weighted mRS at 90 days:** 5.5 (thrombectomy) vs. 3.4 (control); adjusted difference 2.0 points (95% credible interval 1.1–3.0)
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 6% vs. 3% (P = 0.50) — no significant difference
- **90-day mortality:** 19% vs. 18% (P = 1.00) — no significant difference
- Trial stopped early for efficacy at 31 months

**Conclusion:** Thrombectomy plus standard care significantly improved 90-day functional outcomes compared with standard care alone in patients with a clinical–imaging mismatch.

---

### 2. **DEFUSE 3 Trial** (Albers et al., *NEJM* 2018)

**Full title:** *Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging*

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Population:** 182 patients with proximal middle-cerebral-artery or internal-carotid-artery occlusion, last known well 6–16 hours earlier, with a **perfusion–imaging mismatch** ("target mismatch"):
- Initial infarct volume <70 mL
- Ratio of ischemic tissue volume (on perfusion imaging) to infarct volume ≥1.8
- Mismatch volume ≥15 mL

**Intervention:** Endovascular thrombectomy plus standard medical therapy vs. standard medical therapy alone.

**Primary endpoint:** Ordinal score on the **modified Rankin Scale** (0–6) at day 90.

**Key findings:**
- **Favorable shift in mRS distribution:** Odds ratio **2.77** (95% CI 1.63–4.70; P <0.001); adjusted OR 3.36 (95% CI 1.96–5.77; P <0.001)
- **Functional independence (mRS 0–2) at 90 days:** **45%** in the endovascular group vs. **17%** in the medical-therapy group (risk ratio 2.67; 95% CI 1.60–4.48; P <0.001)
- **90-day mortality:** 14% vs. 26% (P = 0.05)
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 7% vs. 4% (P = 0.75) — no significant difference
- Trial stopped early for efficacy after 182 patients (prespecified efficacy boundary P <0.0025 exceeded)

**Conclusion:** Endovascular thrombectomy plus standard medical therapy significantly improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with standard medical therapy alone in patients selected by perfusion imaging mismatch.

---

### Summary Comparison

| Feature | **DAWN** | **DEFUSE 3** |
|---|---|---|
| **Time window** | 6–24 hours | 6–16 hours |
| **Selection criteria** | Clinical–imaging mismatch (age-stratified infarct volume vs. NIHSS) | Perfusion–imaging mismatch (target mismatch: infarct <70 mL, ratio ≥1.8, mismatch ≥15 mL) |
| **N randomized** | 206 | 182 |
| **Functional independence (mRS 0–2)** | 49% vs. 13% | 45% vs. 17% |
| **mRS shift OR** | Not reported as OR (utility-weighted mRS) | 2.77 (95% CI 1.63–4.70) |
| **Symptomatic ICH** | 6% vs. 3% (NS) | 7% vs. 4% (NS) |
| **90-day mortality** | 19% vs. 18% (NS) | 14% vs. 26% (P = 0.05) |

Both trials demonstrated that **imaging-selected patients in the late window derive substantial benefit from mechanical thrombectomy**, with roughly **2.5- to 3-fold increases in the odds of functional independence** and **30+ percentage-point absolute increases** in the rate of mRS 0–2 at 90 days, without increased rates of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage.

The two pivotal randomized controlled trials that established the benefit of imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy in adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion presenting 6–24 hours after last known well are the **DAWN trial** and the **DEFUSE 3 trial**. Both were published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in 2018.

---

## 1. DAWN Trial (2018)

**Full citation:** Nogueira RG, Jadhav AP, Haussen DC, et al. *Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378(1):11-21.

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Time window:** 6–24 hours from last known well.

**Imaging selection criteria:** Clinical-core mismatch defined by age-stratified thresholds:
- Age <80 years: NIHSS ≥10 and infarct volume ≤31 mL
- Age ≥80 years: NIHSS ≥10 and infarct volume ≤51 mL
- Or: NIHSS ≥20 and infarct volume ≤51 mL (regardless of age)

**Patients:** 206 randomized (107 thrombectomy + standard care; 99 standard care alone).

**Primary outcomes:**
1. Mean score on the utility-weighted modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 90 days (range 0 [death] to 10 [no symptoms])
2. Rate of functional independence (mRS 0–2) at 90 days

**Results:**
- **Utility-weighted mRS:** Mean score 5.5 in the thrombectomy group vs. 3.4 in the control group (adjusted difference 2.0 points; 95% credible interval 1.1–3.0; posterior probability of superiority >0.999)
- **Functional independence (mRS 0–2):** 49% in the thrombectomy group vs. 13% in the control group (adjusted difference 33 percentage points; 95% credible interval 24–44)
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 6% vs. 3% (P=0.50)
- **90-day mortality:** 19% vs. 18% (P=1.00)

The trial was stopped early at 31 months because of the results of a prespecified interim analysis.

---

## 2. DEFUSE 3 Trial (2018)

**Full citation:** Albers GW, Thijs V, Wechsler L, et al. *Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging.* N Engl J Med. 2018;378(7):611-621.

**Design:** Multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment.

**Time window:** 6–16 hours from last known well.

**Imaging selection criteria (perfusion mismatch):**
- Proximal MCA (M1) or internal carotid artery occlusion
- Initial infarct volume <70 mL
- Mismatch ratio (ischemic tissue on perfusion imaging / infarct volume) ≥1.8
- Mismatch volume ≥15 mL

**Patients:** 182 randomized (92 endovascular therapy + standard medical therapy; 90 standard medical therapy alone).

**Primary outcome:** Ordinal score on the modified Rankin Scale (mRS 0–6) at 90 days.

**Results:**
- **Ordinal mRS shift:** Favorable shift in the thrombectomy group (unadjusted common odds ratio 2.77; 95% CI 1.63–4.70; P<0.001); adjusted OR 3.36 (95% CI 1.96–5.77; P<0.001)
- **Functional independence (mRS 0–2):** 45% in the endovascular-therapy group vs. 17% in the medical-therapy group (risk ratio 2.67; 95% CI 1.60–4.48; P<0.001)
- **90-day mortality:** 14% vs. 26% (P=0.05)
- **Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage:** 7% vs. 4% (P=0.75)
- **Serious adverse events:** 43% vs. 53% (P=0.18)

The trial was terminated early for efficacy after the first interim analysis exceeded the prespecified efficacy boundary (P<0.0025).

---

## Summary of Key Findings

| Feature | DAWN | DEFUSE 3 |
|---|---|---|
| **Time window** | 6–24 hours | 6–16 hours |
| **Imaging selection** | Clinical-core mismatch (age-stratified) | Perfusion mismatch (core <70 mL, ratio ≥1.8, volume ≥15 mL) |
| **N randomized** | 206 | 182 |
| **Functional independence (mRS 0–2)** | 49% vs. 13% | 45% vs. 17% |
| **Symptomatic ICH** | 6% vs. 3% | 7% vs. 4% |
| **90-day mortality** | 19% vs. 18% | 14% vs. 26% |

Both trials demonstrated that **imaging-selected mechanical thrombectomy significantly improves 90-day functional outcomes** compared with medical therapy alone in late-window anterior-circulation stroke, with no significant increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. These findings established the "tissue window" paradigm—selecting patients based on salvageable tissue rather than time alone—for extended-window thrombectomy.
